frequency_question: How often do U.S. presidents follow through on announced major unilateral trade restrictions within the specified timeline when possessing the direct authority to do so?
membership_rule: Includes explicitly announced unilateral executive tariff or trade restriction threats directed at a specific sovereign trading partner. Excludes statutory congressional tariff bills, multilateral treaties requiring ratification, and vague exploratory rhetoric without formal administrative scheduling.
coverage_note: 7 named major unilateral tariff actions; believed roughly 8 in total meeting exact criteria since 1970.
known_gaps: Minor tactical tariff threats used purely as brief negotiating levers that were immediately dropped are under-counted in historical summaries compared to formalized executive orders.
skeleton: Presidential unilateral trade restriction announcements categorized by final execution versus withdrawal/replacement prior to deadline.
validity_reason: Valid through the duration of the current presidential term, as executive trade authority structures remain constant under existing statutory frameworks.
